items.title: JMGO’s very bright all-in-one projector looks ideal for gamers and sports
items.summary:
JMGO’s Iris Ultra Max 4K 120Hz Google TV projector. | Image: JMGO	

JMGO's 4K 120Hz Iris Ultra Max all-in-one Google TV projector is now available outside China. It gets its name from a new dual-iris system that lets it produce an impressive 10,000:1 native contrast, according to JMGO. It boosts the contrast - always an issue with projectors - by placing two separate physical apertures (irises) along different points of the internal optical path to control light scatter and brightness far more aggressively than a single iris can. It also promises to produce a very bright 6,500 ISO lumen image from its triple-laser light engine.

items.title: FTC lawsuit alleges Amazon has been ‘secretly and systematically’ overcharging for ads
items.summary:
The FTC and 22 state attorneys general are suing Amazon for allegedly using a "secret ad surcharge" to drive up prices for ads on its website and app. FTC chairman Andrew Ferguson claims in a blog post on the lawsuit that the higher advertising prices "were largely passed on to American consumers." According to the complaint, Amazon violated the FTC Act and over a dozen state laws. This lawsuit comes almost a year after Amazon agreed to pay $2.5 billion to settle an earlier FTC lawsuit over Prime subscription practices.

Alienware’s budget-friendly QD-OLED is discounted for the first time
items.summary:
The Alienware AW2726DM is a wallet-friendly screen with premium features for gaming.	

While memory and storage prices are still high, there are still good discounts on other gaming-related hardware. Take Alienware’s AW2726DM, for example. Dell is selling it for $319.99, a $30 break from the usual price of $349.99. The 27-inch gaming monitor features an QD-OLED panel for deep, immersive black levels, and quantum dots for full and vivid colors. With a 240Hz refresh rate for super smooth gaming, and AMD FreeSync Premium Plus to keep your frames per second and refresh rate locked together, this monitor is a great, budget-friendly choice for PC gamers who don’t want to compromise on contrast and fast response times.
Alienware AW2726DM QD-OLED monitor

Where to Buy:

 $349.99 $319.99 at Dell

Connectivity is a bit limited, with a DisplayPort 1.4 port that supports up to 240Hz at 2560 x 1440, and two HDMI ports that support up to 120Hz at its peak resolution. While some other screens have USB hubs or audio connections, they aren’t necessary for PC gaming, and sometimes add to the cost. The included stand has adjustable swivel, height, pivot, and tilt, with a 100 x 100 VESA mount in case you want to mount it to a monitor arm or use a different stand. It also sports a lengthy three year warranty with coverage for burn-in.
Read our Alienware AW2726DM hands-on.

Car owners want tech they can ignore
items.summary:
Automakers keep shoving more tech into their cars, despite evidence that consumers are increasingly fed up with huge screens and glitchy software. In fact, the features that car owners appreciate the most happen to be the ones they barely notice, according to the latest tech survey from JD Power. 
The consumer research firm surveyed 68,084 owners of new 2026 model-year vehicles after 90 days of ownership. The survey touched on 40 automotive technologies covering comfort and convenience; connected vehicles; driver assist; electric vehicles; and smart vehicles.

items.title: Phil Schiller is leaving his biggest jobs at Apple
items.summary:
Longtime Apple executive Phil Schiller is stepping down from his role as the head of the App Store and Apple events, according to a report from Bloomberg. Following the change, Schiller will keep his Apple Fellow title and continue "working on unspecified initiatives," Bloomberg reports.
Schiller initially joined Apple in 1987 and became the company's head of marketing in 1997. He helped launch the App Store alongside Steve Jobs in 2008, but only started heading up the store in 2015. Debian won’t ban AI code from its Linux distribution
items.summary:
Debian voted to allow developers to use AI tools in their contributions to the Linux distribution's "development, maintenance, [and] documentation." The new policy on AI acknowledges that "responsible" use of AI can improve developers' productivity, and goes on to say, "generative AI is neither exempt from nor subject to special rules beyond the standards already expected of Debian contributors."
The project's voting developers considered several other proposals on how to handle AI, including some that would have banned contributions made using AI tools. As It's FOSS reports, some users and contributors aren't happy with the policy, includi …

items.title: Sony’s WH-1000XM5 headphones are back down to their lowest price
items.summary:
Sony is one of many companies offering Labor Day discounts on tech products, though its week-long sale on the last-gen WH-1000XM5 is one of the most attractive deals I found upon logging in this morning. The comfy over-ear headphones offer some of the best sound quality and active noise cancelling, and are down to $198 at Amazon and Best Buy. Originally $399.99, they typically sell for around $250, and this $50 price drop brings them back down their Prime Day 2026 price we saw in late June. However, this time you don’t need a Prime subscription to save.
Sony WH-1000XM5

Where to Buy:

 $399.99 $198 at Amazon
 $399.99 $198 at Best Buy

The XM5 launched in 2022, but don’t let their age fool you into thinking these aren’t great headphones by modern standards. While the newer XM6 from 2025 offer slight improvements to sound and noise cancellation (and brought back the compact folding design from the XM4 and earlier), the XM5 are still a fantastic value. Sony is rumored to be reintroducing its XM4 headphones with a friendlier price tag —they launched in 2020 for $349.99— though it’s doubtful that they’ll be as affordable as the XM5 currently is. Read our review.

Other great Verge-approved deals
Today is your final day to grab a Nintendo Switch 2 at its original $449.99 price. It’ll go up to $499.99 for the base model starting September 1st, and bundles launching this fall will cost up to $549.99. I wouldn’t call it a deal to get one for its usual price today, but it’ll look like one in hindsight. With Nintendo’s controllers and other accessories costing quite a bit a more than their last-gen counterparts, grabbing hardware ahead of the price increase is a smart move. The console is available at Amazon and Best Buy. Alternatively, you can grab a bunch of discounted Nintendo gift cards at Newegg or Costco until you have enough credit added to your Nintendo account to get a system.
The Matic robot vacuum is getting a $250 price increase on September 9th, so this is just a reminder that your time is running low to consider getting one at its original cost. Currently $1,245 through Matic, it’ll rise to $1,495 due to rising costs for memory and other components. Your purchase will come with a year’s worth of replacement bag shipments (a $96 value). Also, Matic has increased its return policy from 60 days to six months. My colleague Jennifer recently tested out Matic Cues, its new gesture and voice control features that further set the Matic out from the crowd of robot vacuums.
Plenty of Sonos gear (in white or black) is discounted at Best Buy ahead of Labor Day. The sale has a home theater focus, and includes the company’s current range of products. Starting with subwoofers, its Sub Mini is down to $399.99 ($100 off) while the more powerful Sub 4 is $759, a $140 price drop. Most of its soundbars are cheaper, too, including the Sonos Arc Ultra for $899 ($200 off) and the Beam Gen 2 for $399 ($100 off). Also, its powerful Era 300 smart speaker that can add some serious power to your entertainment center setup is $379, $100 off. You know the prices are good when the new gear costs about the same as Sonos’ refurbished products (or less, in some cases).
